_note: THE TEMPLATE REGISTRY. One row per ALIAS SHAPE, never per mission.
A template says what a base quest can express and where its moving parts are. Everything in a
row was READ OFF THE RECORD with `gen_inspect qall <base>`, not inferred, and a row is only
added after its base has been read whole.
WHY THIS EXISTS RATHER THAN A C# FILE PER MISSION: the objective layer is Papyrus-only. Of 245
vanilla Default* scripts exactly one touches SetObjectiveDisplayed. So a multi-beat Delve cannot
show its own objectives from records alone, and the only quests that can are ones driven by a
script that already does it. The `driver` field names that script. Choosing a template is
choosing which driver runs the mission, and that is the thing that cannot be authored from data.
TOKENS: a recipe writes <Place> and <Planet>. The generator maps them onto whatever this base
happens to call its aliases, so prose is portable across templates and an author never has to
know that one base says DungeonLocation and another says TargetLocation.

_shape: Pick something up at one marker, carry it to another, hand it over. The driver displays
objective 10 on quest start, gives the player CargoObject on the first activation, displays
objective 20, dresses the second target, and on the second activation REQUIRES the player to
be carrying the cargo before it completes. Without it, FailMessage shows and nothing moves.
THE BASE SHIPS IT ACROSS TWO POIs and this template collapses it into one: both beat markers
are pointed at the same place alias. That collapse is the whole difference between a cargo
run and a Delve, and it costs one integer per beat.
_extraBeats: BEATS BEYOND THE DRIVER'S TWO SLOTS ARE INSERTED BETWEEN THEM, never after. The driver
completes the quest on the second activation, so the LAST beat is always its slot 2 and the
FIRST is always its slot 1. Everything in between gets a freshly created beat slot: a marker
alias filling inside the place, an activator create-obj'd at it, a stage carrying its journal
line, and a stock DefaultAliasOnActivate gated on the previous beat's stage.
⛔ AN EXTRA BEAT CARRIES A JOURNAL AND NO OBJECTIVE. The driver displays objectives 10 and 20
and nothing else, and of 245 vanilla Default* scripts exactly one displays an objective at
all. Measured across his own corpus: 237 quests carry one objective, 92 carry two, NONE
carries three. So an extra beat moves the story and not the on-screen marker, and the lint
refuses an objective on one rather than writing a string nobody will ever see.
